newsitem.title: USA: Hewlett says to look at spending plans.
newsitem.headline: Hewlett says to look at spending plans.

text.p: Hewlett-Packard Co said Monday it needs to bring its expenses into better alignment with market demands, and it will look at spending plans across the company and make adjustments as needed.
The company also said its business strategies and programs are on target.
The company said its third quarter cost of sales increased faster than it has in recent quarters, due in part to steps it took to stimulate demand.
It also said revenue from its medical business was down "significantly" due to shipment delays in some product lines.
These factors kept it from bringing more of its revenue growth to the bottom line.
"While net earnings improved...we're disappointed with our profit outcome," said Lewie Platt, the company's chairman, president and chief executive officer.
The company reported earnings per share for the third quarter of $0.58 compared to $0.40 per share. Analysts consenus for the 1997 quarter was $0.68 per share, according to First Call.

The company said it had expected to see some increase in cost of sales and operating expenses. But lower revenue in its medical business, acquisition effects and higher-than-usual SAR expenses had a greater impact than it expected.
Together, these events reduced its earnings per share by about $0.07.
The company said it is working to achieve the right balance between managing expenses carefully and investing for growth.
The company also said, however, it is pleased with its comeback in order and revenue growth, driven by excellent acceptance of new products and services.
Net revenue for the quarter was $10.5 billion, compared with $9.1 billion in the year-ago quarter. Orders for the quarter were $10.4 billion, a 19 percent increase over last year's third quarter.
The company said it will continue to aggressively pursue its business strategies and targets. It said it has ambitious product introductions planned throughout the company.
It said it is rolling out new services designed to help customers embrace the Internet and manage their distributed computing environments.
